To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

subcutaneously injected nitro-oleate (a nitro–f fatty acid) reduces atherosclerotics lesion formation in apoprotein E–deficiency mice, and that this is due to the anti-inflammatory and anti-oxidant properties of nitro- oleate.

nitro- oleic acid reduces atherosclerosis in apolipoprein E-deficient mice by attenuating tissue oxidant generation and inflammatory cell infiltration, reducing foam cell formation, and conferring plaque stability.

nitro–fats, which are byproducts of nitrite-dependent red-ox reactions of unsatured fatty acids, are potent inhibitors of the development of atherosclerosis in mice, and that they act in a variety of ways to reduce the development of atheromas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of nitro–lipids in atherosclerosis and the potential of this novel class of lipid mediators to serve as therapeutic agents.
the development and application of nitro–alkene chemistry to the study of biological processes.
understanding how nitro–faty acids, which are produced endogenously in vivo, can be used to modulate inflammatory processes in atherosclerosis and other chronic inflammatory diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the nitration of oleic acid by nitric oxide or nitrite, which is formed by the reaction of nitric oxide with O2, leads to the production of nitro-9,10-octadecadienoic acid, which is also known as nitro-oleoic acid, which in turn is capable of reducing atherosclerosis in mice.
NO and NO2 are antiatherogenic, but the NO2- derived nitro-oleoic acids are even more potent in reducing atherosclerotics in mice.
nitro-FA are anti-inflammatory and anti-atherogenic, but the mechanism by which they do so remains to be determined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nitro-fatty acids have anti-atherogenic effects in mice.
nitro-fatty acids, by-products of the reaction between nitric oxide and fatty acids, have anti-inflammatory actions and may have therapeutic potential in the treatment of atherosclerosis.

electrophilic NO adducts of unsaturated fatty acid, which are generated by nitrite-dependent red-ox reactions of unsaturation, have potent anti-inflammatory actions and are effective in reducing atherogenesis in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nitro-FA are potent anti-atherogenic agents in vivo.
nitro–oleic acid is an anti-inflammatory agent that inhibits the formation of atherosclerrotic plaques in the mouse model of atherosclerois.
nitro-fatty acids are potent modulators of vascular inflammation.
